subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Obtain the reduction formula for I_n = ∫ cosⁿx dx and hence find ∫ cos⁴x dx.

mark_split.label: Apply by parts and use cos²x = 1 − sin²x
Substitute n = 4, 2, 0 for the final answer

insider_note: Compare this to 16.1 side by side: the sinⁿ working carries a minus sign from v = −cosx that the cosⁿ working never picks up, because here v = sinx is already positive — that is the whole reason the two final answers differ only in sign pattern, not in structure.

steps.label: Set up integration by parts
lines: Given I_n = ∫ cosⁿx dx = ∫ cosⁿ⁻¹x · cosx dx
steps.why: Exactly the same split as sinⁿx: peel off one cosx to integrate, leave cosⁿ⁻¹x to differentiate.
common_mistakes: Taking v = −sinx by carrying over the minus sign from the sinⁿ working — there is no minus here, since ∫cosx dx = sinx.
Swapping u and v, which stalls the reduction instead of lowering the power.
steps.memory_tip: ∫cosx dx = +sinx (no minus) — that is the one sign difference from the sinⁿ case.

steps.label: Apply by parts and use cos²x = 1 − sin²x
steps.why: Replacing sin²x by 1 − cos²x keeps everything in powers of cosx, closing the loop back to I_n and I_{n−2}.
common_mistakes: Not distributing the (n−1) across both terms once the bracket is expanded.
Writing sin²x = 1 + cos²x by sign slip instead of 1 − cos²x.
steps.memory_tip: The identity always swaps IN the power you don't have (cos²x) for the power you do (sin²x).

steps.label: Solve for the reduction formula
steps.why: Same algebra as sinⁿx — collect the I_n terms and divide by n — but every term here stays positive.
common_mistakes: Carrying a stray minus sign from the sinⁿ derivation out of habit.
Dividing by n on one side only, leaving an inconsistent equation.
steps.memory_tip: This boxed line is the sinⁿ formula with every minus sign erased.

steps.label: Substitute n = 4, 2, 0 for the final answer
lines: I₂ = cosx sinx/2 + (1/2)I₀, and I₀ = ∫dx = x
steps.why: The same even-n chain as sinⁿx — n=4 needs I₂, I₂ needs I₀ = x — but with every sign positive throughout.
common_mistakes: Mixing in a minus sign anywhere, carried by habit from the sin⁴x version done alongside it.
Forgetting the +c at the very end.
steps.memory_tip: sin⁴x and cos⁴x are structural twins — same coefficients (1/4, 3/8, 3/8), opposite name, same sign (all +).
